proof.observed: PASS. Rendered kinds exactly StatefulSet, two Services, ConfigMap, PodDisruptionBudget. Cluster envoy-nats formed in 232ms with a JetStream meta leader; a client with no credential became the session user and was refused a publish to notifications.live. SIGKILL of the R3 stream leader envoy-nats-0 after 205 of 1000 acknowledged messages; envoy-nats-1 led 4.815s later; all 1000 acknowledged messages stored exactly once (8 publish attempts retried); the killed server restarted on its store and all three copies were current at sequence 1000 2.066s later. Exporter: 3 nats_stream_last_seq series at rest, 2 with one server down, 1 for an R1 stream. A user added then removed through an atomically renamed auth.conf: each server logged 'Reloaded server configuration', admitted then refused the user; the client kept server_id and cid 20 with 0 reconnects and 0 disconnects; PIDs unchanged. A session-user change: each server logged 'config reload not supported for NoAuthUser', kept the old session user, and a restarted server took the new one.

deviations: main@origin (sjawhar/legion#2283 and others) was merged into the branch before the first code commit, as plan task 0 says, because the component reuses #2283's priority-class lookup; the skill otherwise reintegrates the base only on a conflict.

Per the INFRA-14 architect (Envoy, 2026-10-27 05:42Z, option C), the branch is stacked on legion/INFRA-546 (forward merge of 0681b1218da2) and the PR's base is legion/INFRA-546, so the bucket-grant test passes against #2362's code.

Plan 1.1's natsMemory floor is divided by 0.8 because nats-server now runs with GOMEMLIMIT at 80% of its memory limit (the chart README's recommendation); without GOMEMLIMIT the heap can grow to about twice its live size and the pod be OOM-killed. INFRA-546's 41 GiB gives 47 / 53 / 5Gi; the architect accepted these.
Plan 4.3's 10 s new-leader bound is 15 s: nats-server v2.15.1's Raft election timeout is a random 4-9 s (server/raft.go:317-318).
Plan 1.3 item 6 puts the advertiser and preStop scripts in the ConfigMap; the shared tailnet_service.go renders them inline for /bin/sh -c, so the ConfigMap holds serve.json alone.
natsReplicas is refused without tailnet (it renders only into the tailnet listener: the owned-input rule); the tailnet pod's total is held to Autopilot's floors like the hub pod's.
openQuestions: The README's disk-growth procedure (orphan-delete the StatefulSet, state delete, recreate) and the PromQL for fewer than three current copies are documented from Kubernetes and exporter behaviour but not exercised on a cluster; the live proof on GKE is dispatch://INFRA-551's.
